Olivia Nguyen: Heads-up: support flagged a customer whose embeddings broke after the v1->v2 swap. They relied on an alias and ended up with 128d vectors, not 1536d.
Matt Chen: Yikes. Which alias? Any repro?
Olivia Nguyen: They used the quickstart which calls embed without a model param (`client.embed({ input })`). If alias resolves to embed_xsmall we get 128.
Raj Patel: OK — immediate fixes: 1) Update quickstart snippets to explicitly pin embedding model id. 2) Add a caveats section in the migration guide about alias fallthrough and dims. 3) CI smoke test to validate vector length for docs snippets.
Sophia Li: I'll draft the migration paragraph and banner copy: "If you previously relied on model aliases, verify embedding model and vector dimensionality after migration; pin model IDs in production."
Matt Chen: I'll update JS/TS/Python quickstarts today. Snippet example: `await client.embed({ model: 'h2o-embed-1536', input: 'hello' })`
Raj Patel: I'll open a small CI PR that runs the embed snippet in staging and asserts len == 1536. Gate failures unless the docs-owner label is set.
Olivia Nguyen: Assigning owners: Sophia (docs PR), Matt (snippet PR), Raj (CI). ETA end of week.
docs-bot: Issue created: "docs: migration - embed alias dimensionality" (#4901)
Matt Chen: Pushed TS + Py snippets to branch `docs/explicit-embed`  waiting review.
Sophia Li: Draft pushed for migration guide. Will add failing repro and a short how-to for reindexing if dims changed.
Raj Patel: CI smoke runner queued. Will post results here.
docs-bot: CI job `docs-embed-dim-check` completed: PASS (1536)
Olivia Nguyen: Thanks team. After merges we'll add a changelog blurb and update the support template.
